method.selection: random.Random("review-2026-10-27:" + audit); two flagged and one unflagged per library, plus two additional flagged targets
method.interpretation: Deliberately enriched for positives, not a prevalence sample. useful_candidate means at least one convincing source-based improvement within the rubric, not agreement with every finding in that file. uncertain requires additional justification or an implementation check. not_justified means the evidence does not justify counting this target under this rubric; it can still contain useful advice under another rubric.
method.validation: Read judgments and relevant source definitions, proof blocks, uses and counterparts. No replacement proof or simplifier claim was compiled or experimentally validated. Negative checks are spot checks, not certificates that no finding exists. No new model inference, rubric changes or data deletion.

targets.review_reason: Classical.decEq is a documented short name with instance_reducible already present. The finding establishes neither substantive duplicated API nor a practical incompatibility; this is an explicitly permitted named wrapper.

IsMaxChain is equivalent to Maximal (IsChain r), but its equality-oriented fields are a defensible specialization. The conversion cost is real but the finding does not establish that changing the representation improves the complete API.
Bundled sheaf constructions are useful named specializations, with no obvious competing-concept defect.

The hand-built rational-map additive/scalar API can plausibly reuse IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom. The alternative base-change witness is proved using of_comp, independently of the original tower equivalence. Preserve the useful names; this supports consolidation of machinery, not deletion of the Hodge-facing API.
The two point equivalences are concrete duplication candidates within TauCeti, but the cited counterpart is not in Mathlib/core/Batteries. This does not meet this audit's specified comparison scope.
The termination predicates are problem-specific; existing relation machinery is reused.
The named Hom equivalence can be implemented using Iso.homCongr, but a short equivalence constructor and its chosen orientation do not establish a competing concept with substantive duplicated API.

The private/public duplicated construction is an internal cleanup, outside the Mathlib comparison. The degree-zero component is a mathematically natural representation; equivalence to a range does not establish that this definition should be replaced.
The target provides dimension theorems using existing definitions.

There is genuine inclusion/projection/orthogonality machinery, but sumPow is deliberately recursive and needs only binary biproducts; the proposed n-ary replacement changes the available assumptions and induction interface. The full refactor needs demonstration.

The canonical coordinate filtration matches the purpose of Mathlib Filtration.piLE, which avoids the extra topology/strong measurability assumptions imposed here. This is a useful integration/generalization candidate. The separate objection to named coordinate wrappers is not justified.
The target supplies theorems about an existing object rather than introducing another concept.
The q-coefficient linear map has a plausible more general replacement in the same FLT project, not in Mathlib. Useful reuse advice can still be outside this rubric.

The handwritten two-by-two trace linear map can use Matrix.traceLinearMap, but its implementation and conversion overhead are small. Repeated sl2M definitions are internal duplication. The finding has useful cleanup potential without establishing the substantive competing-concept cost required here.
The adic/chart normal-form definitions have specialized roles; no obvious competing concept was identified in the inspected material.

The transitivity predicate is introduced in an imported file, not this target. The local environment-cons operation is a short named specialization. Neither supports flagging this target as introducing an avoidable competing concept.

Assignment is a readable predicate subtype whose fields are used directly. Its one cardinality equivalence to powersetCard does not establish a defect in this deliberate representation; the suggested representation also adds a decidability dependency.
The target supplies geometric estimates using imported concepts.

The local finite-dimensionality instance may be redundant with imported instances, but removing it should be tested for inference behavior. It is routine instance setup rather than an established competing mathematical concept.

The existing algSpec functor provides the same object/map construction and can replace repeated morphism/isomorphism commutation proofs in ComponentScheme and ComponentProduct while preserving the names. The object abbreviation alone is not a defect.

The star-convex variants repeat the same endpoint and positivity case analysis. Deriving the more general variant from the positive-coefficient result removes duplicated reasoning with a clear proof shape.
Two power-series radius arguments repeat density, zero/nonzero, NNReal lifting and summability-to-radius reasoning. A shared lemma has a credible mathematical statement and removes both copies.
Componentwise categorical proofs are short structural wrappers.

The repeated quotient-map setup is mostly normality instances and a call to the existing map-surjectivity API. A helper may be convenient but the required nontrivial mathematical reasoning is not established.

Spin and SO share convergence/non-discreteness patterns, but the proposed helpers largely wrap existing continuity, restricted-product and not_isDiscrete lemmas. A useful abstraction is possible; the source alone does not settle whether the added API improves the full proofs.
The repeated norm manipulations are short and occur in different directions.

Some apparent repetition is in deliberate regression tests. Double-opposite transport repeats more substantial setup, but consists mostly of module/instance plumbing. A refactor should demonstrate a benefit beyond routine wrappers.

The repeated category transport proofs are short eqToHom/naturality bookkeeping. Named coherence lemmas may help, but the finding does not establish the nontrivial repeated mathematical argument required by the rubric.
The pairing identities are short wrappers; no substantial duplicated proof was evident.

VertexWeights.eq_of_pos_of_mem_vertexSet redoes a long normalization/extreme-point argument already provided by the earlier indexed theorem. The file already demonstrates subtype reindexing in mem_face_of_pos, giving a credible replacement.

The interior support-function gap proofs visibly repeat the same ball/sign-vector argument, with the weaker norm bound following from the stronger sum-of-absolute-values bound. Other reported mollification/coercivity blocks also offer substantial shared arguments; their complete replacements have not been compiled.
The analytic composition/inverse proofs use related APIs but do not visibly duplicate a substantial argument.

Unit-inverse membership is repeated in small subproofs of one theorem. This looks more like a short existing-API cleanup than nontrivial reasoning repeated across proofs; the appropriate existing valuation-subring lemma should be checked first.

The conversion of a nonnegative real integral equal to one into a lintegral equal to one repeats the same integrability contradiction and integral/lintegral conversion. This is a plausible shared mathematical lemma. The separate instance-plumbing finding does not meet the rubric on its own.
Repeated pullback-projection rewrites are short.

The eventual power-bound/support argument repeats nontrivial steps and contains a redundant second threshold construction. Consolidating that argument has a clear benefit; the separate short bump-support helper is a weaker finding.

Three curve-length variants repeat the measurable pushforward-with-density argument, including the same image/intersection identity and measure extensionality proof. Factoring the measure argument can preserve the distinct analytic hypotheses.
The main rounding argument is given once and uses helpers.

Several coefficient-category variants repeat roughly thirty lines of cone-component identification and section-comparison bookkeeping. The common generic construction supports a substantial shared proof rather than another short wrapper.

The proposed changes are mostly three-line functor-congruence helpers, standard additive-equivalence bundling, and repeated local instances. They may offer small cleanups but do not satisfy this rubric's explicit nontrivial-reasoning requirement.

The coefficient simplification exposes toFinsupp despite the documented abstraction boundary; direct coefficient normal forms are a useful candidate. T_mul has a credible commutation-cycle risk from its syntactic shape, not an observed Lean failure. Removing eval2_C_mul_T merely because its proof is by simp is not justified.

Insertion/union and conditional insertion/intersection identities have plausible canonical simp orientations with supporting analogous APIs. These are concrete annotation candidates, subject to checking the complete simp set.
The two GridLines empty/univ normalization lemmas are appropriate; no obvious additional interface problem in inspected material.

The claim that a theorem specialized to Fintype.ofFinite fails to match other enumerations is speculative without a Lean reproducer. Downstream letI declarations may be needed simply to form the product. Do not count an observed failure here.

Rewriting projectiveNorm to norm can hide the redex for the base-change/unit lemmas. The cited ordinary-norm API lacks the same general counterparts. A concrete rule-priority/orientation or companion-lemma change is worth checking in Lean.
The short derivative calculation does not establish a missing canonical simp interface.

The evidence establishes that several specialized simp rules are derivable from more general rules and have further-simplifiable right-hand sides. It does not establish a bad normal form, cycle, failure or measured cost. Overlap alone is insufficient.

Full application and subtype-value projection rules are a conventional compatible API. The finding identifies overlap but no concrete adverse behavior; a proof-bearing subtype constructor is not by itself an unsuitable simp result.
The target proves a smoothness result without building a new simplification API.
The translation-isometry API lacks canonical zero/application bridges and actual proofs use change to cross the wrapper boundary. Missing simp bridges are a modest concrete interface improvement.

Tagging the existing application lemma could be useful, but the evidence mostly shows an explicit definition unfolding and does not demonstrate an undesirable normal form. The alternative suggestion to delete the lemma is not supported by that argument.
Explicit braiding/reassociation reasoning is intentional; no obvious missing canonical simp rule.

The pullback-lift wrappers lack projection/reassociated simp lemmas, leading consumers to unfold them repeatedly. Fst/snd rules provide concrete canonical expressions without exposing the construction.

Scalar diagonal values of halfModulus2/torusChar2 have direct normal forms and repeated proofs in consumers; centralizing these rules is useful. The separate scalar_comm proof-reuse/direction complaint does not itself establish a simp-interface defect.
The large chart/minimal-prime argument has no obvious additional simp-interface finding in the inspected portions.

slotVertices and neighbors are finite filters with no membership simp API, and consumers manually manipulate mem_filter/univ. Membership iff lemmas have obvious canonical proposition normal forms and concrete uses.

The gammaInverse/logDeriv shared lemma could be useful, but the proposed improvement is mainly explicit-rw API/repeated-proof reuse. Other findings concern unfolding style and broad simp/linarith fragility, without a demonstrated faulty simp interface.
The trace/eigenvalue inequalities use explicit APIs; inequalities do not automatically call for new simp rules.

varianceHermite has recursive zero/one equations without named base-case simp rules, and downstream proofs unfold the recursion. Monomial/application rules for the polynomial-family map are additional concrete normalization candidates.

IntFractPair.of/mapFr lack projection simp lemmas; downstream files explicitly unfold them or locally tag the whole definition simp. Projection rules would expose the intended components while preserving the abstraction.
